data.title: Senores Pharmaceuticals Secures PIC/S GMP Certification For Gujarat Facility
data.description:
The certification from Ukraine’s medicines regulator is expected to expand the company’s regulatory pathway into semi-regulated pharmaceutical markets

Senores Pharmaceuticals Limited has secured Pharmaceutical Inspection Co-operation Scheme (PIC/S) Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) certification for the manufacturing facility of its subsidiary, Ratnatris Pharmaceuticals Private Limited, in Mehsana, Gujarat, on 17 November, 2026, strengthening its regulatory pathway to enter semi-regulated pharmaceutical markets.

The certification was issued by Ukraine’s State Service on Medicines and Drugs Control (SMDC), with the certificate of GMP compliance dated 16 November, 2026, and received by the company on 17 November. The approval covers the facility’s injectable and oral solid dosage manufacturing operations, enabling Senores Pharmaceuticals to expand the reach of its product portfolio and pursue regulatory opportunities across additional markets.

Expanding Market Access

Commenting on the development, Swapnil Shah, Managing Director of Senores Pharmaceuticals, said the certification would open strategic markets that the company had not been able to serve previously. “The PIC/S approval will open many strategic markets that we couldn't serve so far. With approval of both, injectable and oral solids, our diverse and strategic portfolio’s reach will be further enhanced, and will continue to give long term growth and sustained profitability,” Shah said.

PIC/S GMP certification establishes compliance with internationally recognised pharmaceutical manufacturing quality standards and can support companies in pursuing regulatory approvals in markets that rely on recognised GMP inspection frameworks.

The certification is expected to strengthen Senores Pharmaceuticals’ international expansion strategy by providing additional regulatory access for its manufacturing capabilities across injectable and oral solid formulations. With the Mehsana facility receiving the certification, the company aims to broaden its market reach and leverage its manufacturing portfolio to pursue growth opportunities in semi-regulated pharmaceutical markets.

data.title: Ransomware Attacks Jump 20%; Experts Warn Businesses Face A New Threat Baseline
data.description:
Ransomware, data theft and AI-enabled attacks are escalating, while experts warn that cybersecurity investments are failing to keep pace with the evolving threat landscape

A series of cyber incidents targeting organisations across industries in recent weeks has highlighted an intensifying threat landscape, with attacks affecting technology, manufacturing, energy, healthcare, financial services and public infrastructure. From ransomware and data theft to supply-chain compromises, the incidents have exposed how vulnerabilities in third-party services can affect multiple organisations.

The latest incident this week involving digital experience platform Optimizely brought this risk into focus after malicious JavaScript was injected into websites belonging to 178 organisations, including BBC, CNN, Zoom, Salesforce, GitLab, HSBC and IKEA. Discovered on 16 November, the attack exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely's Web Experimentation account sign-up process, allowing an unauthorised party to add malicious code to customer projects.

The scripts were designed to steal payment card information, capture browser cookies and screenshots, and replace cryptocurrency wallet addresses. Optimizely said it had fixed the vulnerability and removed the malicious code. The incident did not establish that the internal networks of all 178 organisations had been breached; the code was delivered through the shared third-party platform.

Steve Vintz, Co-CEO of Tenable, noted that the incident showed how organisations' exposure extended beyond their own networks. "The attack surface no longer ends at the edge of your network. It extends to every external asset and connection you depend on, whoever owns it," he said, adding that exposure management needed to cover assets organisations did not directly own.

Third-party Vulnerabilities Under Scrutiny

The Optimizely incident follows several other cyberattacks and data breaches reported during October and November.In the energy sector, Norwegian oil and gas major Equinor disclosed an ongoing cyberattack on some IT systems on 17 November, while saying its production operations remained unaffected.

In France, attacks on refrigeration control systems affected around 700 supermarket locations, including outlets linked to Casino, Leclerc, Coopérative U, Metro, Carrefour and Intermarché. Japan's retailer Nitori Holdings reported unauthorised access that could have exposed information relating to as many as 37.62 million records.

Taiwanese semiconductor manufacturer TSMC also confirmed a breach involving an unnamed cloud service provider that exposed employee information, but said its own systems and customer data were not compromised.

Other incidents included a breach involving a third-party email distribution service used by the Osaka city government, exposing more than one million email addresses, and a suspected ransomware attack on Osaka Metropolitan University that disrupted internal systems.

Separately, ransomware attacks exploiting vulnerabilities in Microsoft SharePoint servers affected organisations across sectors, including water utilities, telecommunications, regional government and education.

The Numbers Behind The Cyber Surge

While the incidents have received considerable attention, cybersecurity experts said the increase is not merely a consequence of greater media coverage. Threat intelligence data points to a rise in actual cybercrime activity, particularly ransomware.

Mandar Patil, EVP at Cyble, said the company's research arm, Cyble Research and Intelligence Labs (CRIL), recorded 3,836 ransomware attacks globally in the first half of 2026, compared with 3,201 in the same period last year, an increase of around 20 per cent.

The pace accelerated in the following months. August was the most active month of 2026, with 1,034 organisations publicly named as victims by 88 ransomware groups. Attack volumes rose 60 per cent in July and another 25 per cent in August, reversing a three-month decline between March and June.

Patil said the increase was becoming a sustained trend rather than a temporary spike. “We do not read this as a seasonal spike. CRIL treats it as a new baseline, which means security planning based on first-half 2026 volumes is now running about 41 per cent below actual activity.”

"The surge is driven by scale rather than new technology. CRIL attributes it to affiliate recruitment and the exploitation of internet-facing infrastructure, not to new encryption capability, and gangs are using AI to speed up intrusions," Patil added.

Subhajeet Singha, Senior TRU Researcher at Acronis Threat Research Unit, said multiple independent datasets pointed to a rise in cyber incidents, with the scale of exposure increasing alongside the number of breaches.

"Clusit recorded 4,911 serious incidents globally in the first half of 2026, a 71 per cent jump from the same period last year," Singha said. In the US, the Identity Theft Resource Center (ITRC) tracked 1,803 data compromises during the same period, compared with 1,732 a year earlier. However, the number of victim notices crossed 471 million in six months, already exceeding the total recorded for all of 2025.

Singha said the growing use of AI was lowering the barriers to cybercrime, allowing individuals to carry out attacks at a scale that previously required greater resources. "In recent attacks, multiple AI agents have been used by just one individual to make large scale attacks. This makes it easier (in terms of skill and cost) to conduct attacks meaning there are more attackers, and therefore more targets," he added.

Singha also flagged third-party and supply-chain vulnerabilities as major contributors to the rise, as a breach involving a trusted service provider can expose several organisations that depend on its systems.

Why Critical Sectors Are In The Crosshairs

Manufacturing, professional services, IT and IT-enabled services, healthcare and financial services are among the sectors experiencing heightened cyber activity. According to CRIL, manufacturing recorded 151 ransomware victims in August, followed by professional services with 147, IT and IT-enabled services with 126, and healthcare with 98. BFSI was the most affected sector in terms of data breaches during the first half of 2026.

The nature of attacks is also changing, with cybercriminals relying on data theft and extortion rather than encrypting victims' systems. In one CL0P campaign exploiting CVE-2026-12569, more than 40 organisations were reportedly compromised through data theft without file encryption.

Singha said financial services, healthcare, government, manufacturing and critical infrastructure remained attractive targets because of the sensitive information they hold and the disruption that prolonged downtime can cause. He also highlighted the growing use of identity-based attacks, credential theft, supply-chain breaches and the exploitation of unpatched software vulnerabilities.

India Sees Rising Cyber Threats

India is facing a sharp increase in ransomware activity. According to CRIL, the country recorded 45 ransomware incidents in the first quarter of 2026, making it the most targeted country in the Asia-Pacific region. This was a 165 per cent increase over the corresponding period last year. In August, India recorded 24 claimed ransomware victims, accounting for around one-sixth of Asia-Pacific claims and ranking seventh globally.

Patil identified The Gentlemen, Sinobi, Vect, Tengu and CL0P among the groups actively targeting Indian organisations. He also flagged repeat attacks, with organisations often being targeted again after their initial breach became public.

Hacktivist groups focused on the Indian subcontinent have also carried out website defacements, distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks and information operations against government, telecom, media and commercial organisations.

Nitin Jhunjhunwala, Partner at Deloitte India, said India was experiencing similar pressures to global markets, particularly across education, healthcare and manufacturing. "Cyber risk is unquestionably intensifying. We are seeing not only more attacks, but attacks that are faster, cheaper to execute and increasingly AI-enabled," he added.

Jhunjhunwala said AI-driven attacks had risen 56 per cent year-on-year, while education, healthcare and manufacturing accounted for nearly 47 per cent of detected threats in recent Indian telemetry.

Cybersecurity Spending Struggles To Keep Pace

The growing threat landscape is prompting organisations to increase cybersecurity investments, with priorities shifting towards identity security, automation, vulnerability management and faster incident detection.

Jhunjhunwala said financial services, insurance and consumer-facing businesses were increasing investments in these areas. The response was moving away from traditional perimeter security towards "identity, AI-enabled defence, rapid detection and cyber resilience".

Singha said banking and financial services, healthcare, telecommunications and large enterprises were leading the increase in spending, driven by regulatory requirements and the potential cost of security failures. Organisations were prioritising recovery and resilience, identity and access security, round-the-clock monitoring and protection against AI-related risks.

Patil, however, cautioned that higher investments did not necessarily mean organisations were adequately prepared for current threat levels. "Investment is rising, but our data shows many organizations are still budgeting for a threat level that has already passed," he added, arguing that security planning based on first-half ransomware volumes was running about 41 per cent below actual activity.

He recommended risk-based patching of internet-facing systems, phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication for third parties, network segmentation, offline backup testing and monitoring dark web leak sites and access markets.

Indian organisations face growing pressure to strengthen their cyber defences, with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025, setting out a framework for data protection and breach-related obligations.

The DPDP regime is being implemented in phases, with most substantive compliance requirements scheduled to take effect from May 2027. CERT-In directions and sector-specific regulations also add to the compliance requirements.

However, the response remains uneven. While larger companies are strengthening their security strategies, limited budgets and a shortage of skilled personnel continue to leave mid-sized businesses and SMEs exposed. Ensuring that regulatory compliance translates into stronger security measures and faster recovery from attacks remains a key challenge.

Aditi Das

BW Reporters The author is a Trainee Correspondent at BW Businessworld. She is a postgraduate with a passion for research and storytelling. Curious by nature, she enjoys writing and exploring new ideas and perspectives.

data.title: South Korea becomes fourth country globally to hit $1 trillion exports on AI chip boom
data.description:
South Korea's exports so far for this year have exceeded $1 trillion, driven by a global AI chip boom, making it the fourth country in the world to reach the milestone after Germany, the United States and China.

Exports passed the $1 trillion mark as of 0509 GMT on Thursday, compared with last year's record of $709 billion, the trade ministry said.

Asia's fourth-largest economy, home to leading chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix , is riding the global boom in AI investment that is fuelling exports and investments.

Still, domestic demand remains weak with the benefits of the export boom yet to trickle down to many households. Consumer sentiment has been hurt by high interest rates and prices, as well as unprecedented volatility in the domestic stock market.

"Now, we need to turn this achievement into sustainable growth. We will enhance the competitiveness of major industries and grow future growth engines, such as AI and bio," President Lee Jae Myung said in a social media post on X.

"Most of all, the achievement in exports should improve the lives of the people. We will create 'growth for all', sharing the opportunities and fruits of growth with big and small companies as well as the capital area and regional areas," Lee said.

The Lee administration plans to create a 162.3 trillion won ($121.94 billion) Future Response Fund to funnel excess tax revenue from the chip boom toward growth industries, young people, regional development and education.

South Korea's economic growth is expected to quicken to the mid-3% range this year on record chip exports, after expanding 1% last year, the country's finance minister said last month.

($1 = 1,330.9700 won)

data.description:
(06:00 GMT) *Novartis Expects Sales to Grow 5% at Constant Currency Through 2031
(06:01 GMT) *Novartis Sees Core Operating Profit Margin on Track to Return to Above 40% by 2029
(06:02 GMT) *Novartis Raises Peak Sales Guidance for Kesimpta, Scemblix and Leqvio
(06:02 GMT) *Novartis Had Previously Targeted Annual Sales Growth of 5%-6% Over 2025-30 Period
(06:03 GMT) *Novartis Sees Kesimpta Peak Annual Sales at $8B, Up From $6B Previously
(06:04 GMT) *Novartis: Scemblix Peak Sales Guidance Raised From $4B to $5B
(06:04 GMT) *Novartis: Leqvio Peak Sales Guidance Raised From $4B to $5B
(06:05 GMT) *Novartis Says It Now Has Nine In-Market Assets With Peak Sales Potential of $3B-$10B
(06:06 GMT) *Novartis: Drug Pipeline Expected to Support Sustained Mid-Single-Digit Growth Long Term
(06:24 GMT) Novartis Sees Sales Growth Through 2031

By Adria Calatayud

Novartis forecast steady sales growth through 2031, citing momentum from drugs already in the market and upcoming launches, and said medicines it has in the pipeline would help it sustain growth over the long term.

The Swiss drugmaker said Thursday that it expects annual sales growth of 5% from 2026 to 2031, excluding the effect of currency movements. It had previously forecast annual sales growth in the 5% to 6% range over the 2025-30 period.

Novartis raised its peak sales estimates for key drugs Kesimpta, Scemblix and Leqvio, saying this reinforces confidence in the company's midterm outlook.

The company said it now has nine in-market products with potential to generate annual peak sales of between $3 billion and $10 billion, as well as 10 in late-stage development that could bring in multibillion-dollar sales at their peak.

Novartis also said it is on track to return to a core operating profit margin above 40% by 2029, as previously indicated.

data.title: A2 Milk Cuts H1 Revenue View, Backs Outlook For H1 EBITDA Margin, FY27; Shares Down
data.description:
CANBERA (dpa-AFX) - a2 Milk Company Ltd. or a2MC (ACOPF, A2M.AX) on Thursday announced that it has trimmed revenue outlook for first half of fiscal 2027, amid the ongoing China Infant Milk Formula or IMF recovery efforts. Further, the firm maintained its outlook for first-half EBITDA margin as well as fiscal 2027.

At its Annual Meeting, the New Zealand-based dairy company also provided an update on its China IMF recovery plan.

In New Zealand, the shares traded 9.70 percent lower, and closed Thursday's trading at NZ$8.01.

Looking ahead for the first half, the company continues to project EBITDA margin to be materially down from last year. Meanwhile, revenues are now expected to be slightly lower year-over-year, while previous view was for revenue to be broadly in line with the prior year.

Further, for fiscal 2027, a2MC said it continues to expect revenue and EBITDA to grow in fiscal 2027, supported by increased contribution from product innovation and new markets, continued momentum in Other Nutritionals and Liquid Milk, and a2 Pokeno profitability improvement.

The firm still projects mid-single-digit percentage revenue growth and Underlying EBITDA margin of approximately 15 percent.

At this stage, the Company still expects total IMF sales to be broadly similar to fiscal 2026.

China label and English label are expected to gradually recover over the course of the new year, supported by the recent launches of two new China label products and the updated a2 Platinum product, and pending resolution of the China importation requirements currently impacting a2 Genesis.

The firm noted that IMF recovery will be supported by an increase in marketing, particularly in the first half. As a result, Group revenue and EBITDA are expected to be materially weighted to the second half of fiscal 2027.

The company previously expected China label to gradually recover over the course of fiscal 2027, and English label offtake momentum to improve during the first half, supported by an increase in marketing particularly in the first half.

The Company, as announced earlier, was impacted by shortfalls of China label IMF product that materially impacted in-market product availability during the fourth quarter. The issue necessitated a large proportion of existing users to switch to alternative brands, with the flow-on effects expected to impact IMF sales in fiscal 2027.

In addition, English label IMF offtake in the fourth quarter was indirectly impacted by the USA label IMF recall announced in May 2026.

Regarding the execution of its China IMF recovery plan, the company noted that so far, estimated China label offtake has recovered to around 50 percent of pre-supply chain disruption levels, up from around 40 percent in August 2026.

data.title: Time For Copper-Focused BHP to Show How It Can Grow — Analysis
data.description:
By Rhiannon Hoyle

ADELAIDE, Australia--A year ago, BHP Group abandoned a bid for Anglo American, reassuring investors it had plenty of options to produce more copper as global demand for the metal swells.

Now the world's most valuable miner needs to show it can deliver.

Copper has become a hot property as investors pour billions into building data centers, making electric vehicles and upgrading power grids. Copper prices hit a record high of $6.8035 per pound on Comex in September, although the market has been volatile lately as Nvidia's leadership turmoil and security concerns deal a blow to the artificial-intelligence trade.

On Monday, BHP begins a two-day investor tour of its Australian copper operations that analysts say could be the single biggest contributor to the company's growth in copper over the coming decade.

The visit to the operations, which are known collectively as Copper South Australia and comprise three mines, processing facilities and an exploration project, could be a chance to build investor confidence in the company's plans.

BHP has "set out an enticing copper growth story," helping its stock outperform many peers year to date, UBS said recently. The miner is betting the world's demand for copper will be reshaped by powerful long-term trends, including the AI boom.

But even BHP acknowledges that copper mines are harder to develop than before. Analysts expect its copper production will drop in the next two years as the business mines less copper-rich ore at pits in Chile.

"While BHP is a good operator, we see challenges with its copper growth," UBS said.

BHP has long wanted to transform its Australian assets, built from acquisitions in 2005 and more recently in 2023, into a business that ranks among the largest in the world.

However, those plans have been delayed for years by high costs and complex geology.

At the heart of Copper South Australia lies the mine and processing facilities of Olympic Dam, one of the world's biggest known deposits of copper, gold and uranium.

Back in 2012, BHP abandoned a proposed expansion that would have turned the underground mine there into a giant open pit for a cost that some analysts estimated to be close to $30 billion.

Helped by the 2023 takeover of copper miner Oz Minerals, BHP more recently developed a plan for a staged expansion of its smelting and refining capacity and its mines to create what it says could be a globally significant mine-to-metal copper province.

BHP aims to make a final investment decision on a major smelter and refinery expansion in 2027, with other possible projects to follow. RBC Capital Markets estimates a first phase of development--including the smelter and refinery project, and expansions at both its Olympic Dam and Carrapateena mines--to cost about $11.6 billion.

Importantly, BHP has improved the reliability of operations at Olympic Dam, which was for years beset by operational instability and external infrastructure constraints, weighing on returns, analysts say.

Last fiscal year, Olympic Dam recorded its highest copper production in more than two decades.

Still, investors are cautious about how quickly the miner can meet its goals.

BHP wants the Australian operations to produce about 500,000 metric tons of copper annually by 2035, up 56% on the 320,700 tons produced in the year through June. It is targeting annual production of up to 650,000 tons by 2040.

The market forecasts output of around 400,000 tons in 2035, 20% below the miner's target, according to Visible Alpha.

"Consensus does not yet have conviction in the production," said Bank of America.

Analysts say that could change once they get a closer look at BHP's plans for the operations. Investors will be seeking greater detail on costs, timing and obstacles to delivering the projects during the visit.

"Evidence of progress… should improve investors' confidence in the pathway," Citi said.

Write to Rhiannon Hoyle at rhiannon.hoyle@wsj.com

data.title: KKR Invests in India Renewables Business Run by Petronas-Backed Gentari
data.description:
By Fabiana Negrin Ochoa

Investment firm KKR has made a minority investment in a renewable-energy platform in India run by Gentari, an entity established by Malaysia's national oil and gas company.

The investment will provide growth capital to support the renewables platform's continued expansion in India, KKR and Gentari said Thursday.

No terms were disclosed.

KKR has been investing in India's infrastructure sector for more than a decade, and has committed more than $27 billion to energy-transition and renewables infrastructure globally since 2011.

The deal with Gentari--part of Petronas Group--aims to capture the need for continued investment in India's energy infrastructure as demand for reliable power grows rapidly.

"We believe scaled platforms that can deliver increasingly sophisticated renewable energy solutions will have an important role to play in meeting that demand," said Hardik Shah, Asia-Pacific infrastructure partner at KKR.

Gentari's India platform has about 8 gigawatts of operating, under-construction and contracted renewable-energy capacity. Its portfolio spans solar, wind, hybrid and battery-energy storage solutions.

Gentari Group Chief Executive Sushil Purohit said that with KKR's support, it is well-positioned to keep scaling the business.

Following the investment, Gentari will retain strategic oversight and operational control of the platform, the companies said.

The tie-up comes on the heels of KKR's roughly $16 billion partnership with RWE investing in offshore-wind farms in the U.K.

Write to Fabiana Negrin Ochoa at fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com

data.title: Square Australia and NAB Team Up to Make Business Simpler
data.description:
Square Australia and National Australia Bank (NAB) are teaming up to make banking and payments simpler for Australian businesses and give them greater control over their cash flow.

For small businesses, including those in retail and hospitality, cash flow matters, margins matter and time matters. The partnership combines NAB’s business banking expertise with Square’s leading payments and business tools to make it easier for customers to manage the everyday work of running a business.

Initially, the partnership will provide eligible NAB customers using Square access to Square’s flexible transfer feature, giving them more control over when their available funds are sent to their NAB Business Transaction Account.

From February next year, businesses can set a close of day time for each day of the week, with Square initiating the transfer of their available funds to their NAB Business Transaction Account 15 minutes later.

NAB Group Executive Business and Private Banking Andrew Auerbach said the partnership reflected the bank’s ambition to keep supporting customers to make running their business easier.

“Many hospitality and retail businesses don’t operate nine to five,” Mr. Auerbach said.

“A restaurant might finish trading late at night and need to pay suppliers the next morning. A café might need to buy tomorrow’s produce, so their banking and payments need to work around how they do business.

“NAB already supports businesses of all shapes and sizes across Australia. We want to keep raising the bar by finding practical ways to make running them easier.

“These sound like small things, but they can make a big difference when you’re running a business. Flexible transfer is the first Square feature being made available through the partnership and we want to build on it.”

Block Global Partnerships Lead Morgan Kuntze said the partnership combined Square’s technology and understanding of sellers with NAB’s expertise in business banking.

“Square works with businesses every day, helping them take payments and manage the day-to-day work that sits behind making a sale,” Ms. Kuntze said.

“By partnering with NAB, we can connect that experience more closely with banking and find new ways to make managing money simpler for sellers.

“Flexible transfer is the first step. Sellers can set their close of day schedule around the way their business operates, and Square automatically initiates the transfer of their available funds.”

For Axil Coffee Roasters, which has grown from a single Hawthorn cafe to more than 16 locations and hundreds of wholesale partners, managing cash flow is part of the everyday reality of running a growing hospitality business.

“There’s no standard working day in hospitality,” said Axil Managing Director David Makin.

“Some of our venues open incredibly early, others trade later, and every day we’re managing staff, stock and suppliers across the business.

“Being able to set our transfer schedule around how we actually trade gives us another level of control over our cash flow.

“We need the flexibility. The more our banking and payments can fit around how the business actually operates, rather than the other way around, the better.”

Through the partnership, NAB and Square plan to build on flexible transfer by exploring further ways to connect banking and payments, simplify cash flow and make it easier for Australian businesses to operate and grow.

NAB has opened up the ability for businesses to express interest in the partnership ahead of the full launch in early 2027 - click here for more information.

Notes to editors:

  • NAB’s current standard settlement time is 9.30pm AEST daily.

  • Square’s flexible transfers require a linked and eligible NAB Business Transaction Account. The availability of funds in the linked bank account may be affected by NAB processing requirements.

  • Square applies transfer limits ranging from $5 to $50,000 AUD per day (new sellers are limited to $5,000 AUD per day until eligible for a higher limit). Flexible Transfers may not be available in limited circumstances beyond Square’s control, including where the linked bank account is not eligible for real-time payments or where there is downtime or delay affecting the New Payments Platform. Square’s Terms of Service apply.

About Square
Square helps businesses turn transactions into connections and businesses into neighbourhood favourites. In 2009, Square started with a simple invention — the first mobile card reader, which changed how the entire financial system thinks about small businesses. Square has since grown into a global business platform helping millions of sellers of all sizes participate and thrive in their communities. Whether independently run or a global chain, Square understands that sellers succeed when they have the freedom to focus on the experiences that keep customers coming back. From point of sale and payments to online commerce, staff management, cash flow tools, and more, Square brings together the tools sellers need to run and grow on one intelligent platform. For more information, visit squareup.com.

About NAB

At National Australia Bank (NAB) Group, our ambition is to be the most customer-centric company in Australia and New Zealand. More than 41,000 colleagues at the bank provide 10 million customers with secure, easy and reliable banking services. About 88% of the Group’s workforce are located in Australia and New Zealand, while others work in Asia, London, New York and Paris. NAB is proud to be Australia’s largest business lender. We stand by our customers, and they have our ongoing support.

data.title: Com7's 4Q Earnings Outlook Appears Positive — Market Talk
data.description: Com7's 4Q earnings outlook appears positive, Maybank Securities (Thailand)'s Wasu Mattanapotchanart says in a research report. Drivers include strong sales of iPhones such as 18 Pro Max and launches of 11 Android smartphone models and of laptops including a touchscreen MacBook Pro, the analyst says. The IT chain store operator's 4Q net profit will likely grow 25% from a year earlier, the analyst estimates. For 2027, the Thai company preliminarily aims for at least 10% revenue growth for its core IT retail business, driven by full-year benefits of higher average selling prices. The brokerage has a buy rating and a target price of 36.50 baht on the shares, which are 0.7% lower at 30.20 baht. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

data.title: PANW Stock Surges 8% Overnight: Palo Alto Networks CEO Sees ‘Hundreds Of Billions Of Dollars’ Opportunity In Open-Weight AI Models Security
data.description:
Key points:
  • CEO Nikesh Arora said open-weight AI models’ share of token usage has climbed from below 5% to over 60% in a year. 
  • Palo Alto Networks has bought Applied Compute for $4.5 billion to strengthen its AI security business. 
  • The company plans to develop over 35 AI-powered security applications and deliver sovereign open-weight models. 

Palo Alto Networks (PANW) stock jumped 8% overnight after a third-quarter (Q3) earnings beat, as CEO Nikesh Arora highlighted a market worth billions for securing open-weight AI models. Speaking on the Q3 earnings call, Arora outlined the company's Applied Compute acquisition, which aims to expand enterprise AI security and bring in $1 billion in annual recurring revenue by fiscal 2029.

Palo Alto Networks’ stock is on track for a second straight weekly gain.

PANW CEO Sees Open Weight AI Models Gaining Enterprise Interest

Arora said during the Q3 earnings call that businesses are opting for AI models that give them greater ownership and control over their technology. Open-weight models have gained traction, making up more than 60% of token usage, compared with less than 5% a year earlier.

“When organizations put AI at the center of their operations, they want to retain control of their proprietary data, institutional judgment and competitive edge inside their own 4 walls. We expect a future with a serving opportunity in the hundreds of billions of dollars when enterprise applications are driven by open weight and open source adoption.”

Applied Compute To Support Palo Alto Networks’ AI Security Expansion

To address the enormous security opportunity, Arora said Palo Alto Networks examined potential partners across the AI industry before selecting Applied Compute, citing its engineering capabilities and experience in developing open-weight models through post-training. Palo Alto Networks agreed to acquire Applied Compute in an all-stock deal valued at $4.5 billion.

The Palo Alto-Applied Compute deal will focus on two things. Networks plans to integrate AI into its existing cybersecurity products, developing more than 35 specialized applications that will help customers counter AI-led threats with AI-driven defenses.

The second focus will be developing and delivering secure, sovereign versions of open-weight models for enterprise customers. “To support our efforts, we plan to build out a diversified global influence capability of north of 100-plus megawatts over the next 3 to 5 years,” Arora said.

“This will be supported by a modest CapEx commitment at least – of less than $3 billion through fiscal 2030, representing approximately half a year of our annual free cash flow.”

PANW Stock: Retail Stance

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock improved to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ territory. The stock recorded an 884% surge in message volume over the past 24 hours.

A user said, “Applied Compute acquisition to bolster PANW’s enterprise capabilities in open-weight AI models.”

Another user said, “$PANW agreed to pay $4.5B in stock for Applied Compute, which helps companies customize and run AI models. That’s a pretty big bet that the folks who buy their cybersecurity will also trust them to help run the models. I’d like to see how many customers sign up for both.”

PANW stock has gained 84% year-to-date.
